title: Why Educators Leave Subscription Platforms (2026 Fee Check)
description: Fixed fee or pay-as-you-sell? Why educators move off subscription platforms, with Classplus, Learnyst, Edmingle and Exly prices from official sites and a cost chart.
og_description: A fair look at why some educators leave subscription course platforms: fixed yearly fees vs pay-as-you-sell pricing, with prices checked on each official site on 24 Oct 2026 and the sales level where each model wins.

h1: Why Educators Are Leaving Subscription Platforms in 2026: Fixed Fees vs Pay-as-You-Sell, Priced Fairly
dek: Some educators move from fixed-fee course platforms to plans that charge mostly when they sell. This guide explains why, compares both pricing models with prices from each official site, and shows when a fixed fee is still the better deal.
cover_alt: Why educators leave subscription platforms: fixed fee versus pay-as-you-sell pricing compared for Classplus, Learnyst, Edmingle, Exly and AllCoaching, prices checked 24 Oct 2026
audience: Indian educators and coaching owners on, or choosing, a subscription course platform
intro: Educators usually leave subscription platforms because a fixed fee is paid before any student has paid them, and in a slow year that fee eats a large share of what they earn. Pay-as-you-sell pricing, where most of the cost is a percentage of sales, moves the cost to when money is actually coming in. But it is not always cheaper: once your sales are high, a fixed fee can cost less.

So the real question is not "subscription or not". It is which pricing model fits your sales today and next year. This guide compares the two models with prices from each platform's own website, checked on 24 Oct 2026, and computes where each one wins.

We are AllCoaching, and our own plans sit in between: a yearly plan from ₹6,999 plus a fee on sales. Read this knowing who wrote it. We say plainly where a fixed-fee plan, or another pay-as-you-sell platform, costs less than ours.
takeaways: A fixed-fee platform charges the same whether you sell or not; a pay-as-you-sell platform charges mostly when you sell.
Classplus lists ₹29,999 for 1 year and ₹39,999 for 2 years on its own pricing page (checked 24 Oct 2026); GST, any fee on sales and renewal price are not stated.
Edmingle starts at ₹7,499 a month billed annually and Learnyst's 0%-fee Professional plan at ₹8,099 a month billed annually; taxes extra on both.
Exly Starter has no upfront fee and takes a 10% commission; its mobile app and custom website are paid add-ons from ₹60,000 a year each.
AllCoaching is a small yearly plan plus a fee: Starter ₹6,999 + 10%, Growth ₹12,999 + 7.5%, Pro ₹24,999 + 5%, Scale ₹59,999 + 0%; GST extra, 14-day free trial with no card.
On published prices, AllCoaching costs less than Classplus up to about ₹2.3 lakh of sales a year; above that, Classplus's listed price is lower on paper.
Pay-as-you-sell is not always cheaper. Check your real sales, then pick the model that costs least at that level.

sections.html:
A fixed fee suits an educator with steady, high sales. Pay-as-you-sell suits an educator who is starting, growing or selling in seasons, such as before NEET or SSC exam dates. Pick the row that sounds like you.

sections.h2: How we compared subscription and pay-as-you-sell platforms
sections.html:
We compared platforms Indian educators commonly use or shortlist, grouped by how they charge: fixed fee (Classplus, Edmingle, Learnyst Professional), pay-as-you-sell (Exly Starter, Learnyst Launcher) and small plan plus fee (AllCoaching). We looked at four things.

  1. The published price, taken only from each company's own pricing page.
  2. The fee on your sales, because a percentage changes the total as you grow.
  3. What is extra: taxes, app, website or other add-ons the page lists.
  4. What is not stated, phrased as a question to ask the vendor.
Disclosure: AllCoaching publishes this guide. Competitor figures link to their official pages and carry the date we checked them (24 Oct 2026). Earlier versions of this article used cost ranges we could not source; we have removed them. Prices change; check the source before you decide. If you spot an error, write to contact@allcoaching.in and we will correct it.

Subscription platforms are not bad products. Most do what they promise: host courses, run live classes, take payments and give you an app. The reasons educators move are usually about how the price fits their income.

1. The fee comes before the first sale

A fixed yearly fee is paid in full at the start. For a new SSC maths tutor or a yoga teacher building a first batch, that can be most of the first year's income. A model that charges mostly on sales means a slow month costs little.

2. Teaching income is seasonal

Exam educators sell most courses in the months before an exam. A fixed fee is the same in a busy month and in a quiet one, so in a quiet year it costs more per rupee earned.

3. The total is hard to see upfront

Some pricing pages leave out GST, any fee on sales, the renewal price or the cost of the app. None of that is wrong on its own, but it makes the true yearly cost hard to compare. Ask for each one in writing before you renew.

{{q:Is the subscription model the problem, or my platform?|Usually neither on its own. A fixed fee is a good deal at high, steady sales and a poor one at low or uneven sales. If your sales have changed since you signed up, the model that fits you may have changed too.}}

4. Wanting to own and change things yourself

Many educators now want their own domain, their own app and the ability to change a price or add a course in minutes, without a request to the vendor. That pushes them toward self-serve academy platforms, whatever the pricing model.

{{fig:before-after|Before and after: a fixed fee paid upfront, renewal price not stated, GST unclear and the app as an add-on, compared with a small yearly plan, a fee only on sales, own app and domain included and published prices|The goal is a price you can see in full before you sign up.}}

sections.html:
Here is each platform as its own company describes it, with the published price, what to check, and who it suits best.

Our platform · disclosure

1. AllCoaching (small plan + fee)

Good at
An academy you build yourself, like Shopify for coaching: website on your own domain, your own Android app (iOS app on Pro and Scale), courses, tests, unlimited live classes and UPI checkout in one studio.
Published price
Starter ₹6,999/yr + 10% on sales, Growth ₹12,999/yr + 7.5%, Pro ₹24,999/yr + 5%, Scale ₹59,999/yr + 0%; GST extra. Pricing[6]
Free trial
14 days, no card needed.
Check
It is still a yearly plan, not a free tier, and the percentage adds up as you grow.
Best for
Educators who want their own brand and a cost that rises mainly with sales.

2. Classplus (fixed fee)

Good at
A branded teaching app and website for coaching businesses; its page says "Get your own brand's teaching app, create your own website & sell courses".
Published price
₹29,999 for 1 year and ₹39,999 for 2 years.[1]
Check
GST, any fee on sales, the renewal price and iOS app availability are not stated on the pricing page; ask in writing.
Best for
Institutes with steady sales well above ₹2.3 lakh a year that want a flat price.

3. Edmingle (fixed fee)

Good at
An "AI-powered LMS purpose-built for professional training and skilling businesses", with batches, branches and white-labelled academies.
Published price
Core ₹7,499/month, Prime ₹14,999/month, Power ₹29,999/month, billed annually; taxes extra; 7-day free start.[3]
Check
The page does not state a fee on sales; its FAQ says some advanced options or higher usage tiers may be priced separately.
Best for
Training businesses with large, steady enrolments.

4. Learnyst (both models)

Good at
Courses, mock tests and live classes, with test series; it offers "Features required to market and sell your content online".
Published price
Launcher ₹10,000/yr + 10% of sales (pay-as-you-sell); Professional ₹8,999/month, or ₹8,099/month billed annually, with 0% transaction fees (fixed fee); taxes extra.[2]
Check
Apps are published under Learnyst's developer account, and a branded Android app starts from Premium.
Best for
Test-series academies; it lets you move from a fee on sales to a fixed fee as you grow.

5. Exly (pay-as-you-sell)

Good at
Storefront, payments, CRM and WhatsApp/email automation for coaches; it calls itself "an all-in-one solution to all things business".
Published price
Starter: no annual upfront fee + 10% commission; Pro ₹30,000/yr + 6%; Premium ₹1,08,000/yr + 3%. Add-ons include a mobile app (iOS and Android) from ₹60,000/yr and a custom website from ₹60,000/yr.[4]
Check
GST treatment is not stated; add the add-ons you need to the plan price.
Best for
Coaches selling sessions and courses who do not need their own app yet.

6. Teachmint and Graphy

Good at
Teachmint now leads with Teachmint X, an AI-powered connected classroom device. Graphy is an all-in-one platform for creators and coaches.
Published price
Teachmint: not listed on its website (checked 24 Oct 2026); you book a demo.[5] Graphy publishes plans on graphy.com/pricing, but prices are shown by country and we could not confirm the Indian rupee plans on 24 Oct 2026; check the page from India.[7]
Check
Ask each for the yearly total, any fee on sales and what the app costs.
Best for
Teachmint: schools needing classroom tools. Graphy: creators selling to their own audience.

sections.h2: When fixed fees win, and when pay-as-you-sell wins
sections.html:
The chart adds each published plan price to its published fee on sales at five sales levels, and picks the lowest-cost plan each time. This is where the two models really differ.

{{fig:cost|Total yearly cost at ₹0 to ₹10 lakh of sales from published prices for AllCoaching, Classplus, Learnyst and Exly|Before GST. Classplus's line is its listed price only, because its pricing page does not state a fee on sales. Exly add-ons not included.}} {{cost_table}}

The honest reading:

  • Against a fixed fee: AllCoaching costs less than Classplus's listed price up to about ₹2.3 lakh of sales a year. Above that, Classplus is lower on paper, provided it confirms there is no fee on sales.
  • Against pure commission: Exly costs less than AllCoaching up to about ₹5 lakh of sales a year, because Exly Starter has no upfront fee. Above that, AllCoaching Pro's 5% is lower. If you need Exly's mobile app add-on (from ₹60,000 a year), AllCoaching costs less at every level in this chart.
  • Against a 0%-fee plan: Learnyst Professional, billed annually, costs ₹97,188 a year before taxes. AllCoaching's own 0% plan, Scale, is ₹59,999 a year.

Edmingle Core works out to ₹89,988 a year billed annually, before taxes; we left it off the chart to keep it readable. Use our plan finder to run your own numbers.

{{cta}}

Starting out (under ₹1 lakh a year)

Keep fixed costs low. A pay-as-you-sell plan or a small yearly plan with a fee lets you test demand before paying much. Our guide to selling online courses without a monthly bill covers the options.

Growing (₹1–5 lakh a year)

Compare the total at your real sales, not the headline price, and include the app and website you need. See how to price online courses in India to set fees that cover your platform cost.

Established (well above ₹5 lakh a year)

Lower percentages and fixed fees start to win. Weigh that against ownership and how easily you can change things yourself. Our best LMS for coaching institutes guide compares more options.

Paying for a platform but not earning yet

Fix the student side first. Read paying for a coaching app but not earning before you change platforms.

sections.h2: How to leave a subscription platform without losing students
sections.html:
The safe way to switch is to run both platforms side by side until your current plan ends. Current students stay where they are until their batch ends; new admissions go to your new academy.

{{fig:switch|Four steps to leave a subscription platform: check your renewal date, build your new academy, move new admissions, close the old plan at renewal|Nobody loses access, and nobody pays twice.}} {{steps}}

We changed our own pricing in 2026 from one model to three published yearly plans, so we know how much a pricing page shapes an educator's decision. Whatever you choose, put the renewal date in your calendar and read the renewal terms before it arrives. The full checklist, including messages to send students, is in how to switch coaching apps without losing students.

items: Check your renewal date and terms
Find when your current plan renews and ask the vendor in writing about notice, refunds and data export.
Start the 14-day trial, connect your domain and upload one complete course with its demo lesson.
Send new admissions to your academy
Share your own website and app link in WhatsApp, YouTube and Instagram for every new batch.
Export records and close the old plan
Download student and payment records, then let the old plan end at renewal.

faq: Why are educators leaving subscription platforms?

Mostly because a fixed fee is paid before any sales, and in a slow or seasonal year it takes a large share of income. Some also want their own domain and app, or a price page that shows GST, fees and renewal in full. Subscription platforms still suit educators with high, steady sales.
What does a subscription course platform cost in India?

Published prices vary. Classplus lists ₹29,999 for 1 year and ₹39,999 for 2 years. Edmingle starts at ₹7,499 a month billed annually and Learnyst Professional at ₹8,099 a month billed annually, both plus taxes. Teachmint does not list prices. All checked 24 Oct 2026.
What is the difference between a subscription platform and pay-as-you-sell?

A subscription platform charges a fixed fee whether you sell or not. A pay-as-you-sell platform charges mainly a percentage of each sale, so you pay more when you earn more and little when you do not.
Is pay-as-you-sell always cheaper than a subscription?

No. At low sales it is usually cheaper; at high sales a fixed fee can cost less. On published prices, AllCoaching costs less than Classplus up to about ₹2.3 lakh of sales a year, and Classplus is lower on paper above that.

Partly. AllCoaching has a yearly plan, from ₹6,999 (Starter) to ₹24,999 (Pro), plus a 10%, 7.5% or 5% fee on sales, with GST extra and a 14-day free trial. It is not a free tier, but most of the cost moves with your sales.
What should I do if I am locked into a yearly subscription?

Use the time. Build your new academy during the 14-day trial, keep current students where they are, send new admissions to your own website and app, and let the old plan end at renewal. Ask your vendor in writing about notice periods and data export.
Will my students follow me if I switch platforms?

They follow your brand more than the platform. If your academy uses your own domain and app, and you tell students early, current batches finish where they are and new students join you on the new academy.
Which platforms charge no upfront fee?

Exly Starter lists no annual upfront fee with a 10% commission, checked 24 Oct 2026; its app and custom website are paid add-ons. AllCoaching is not upfront-free: it starts at ₹6,999 a year after a 14-day free trial.
glossary: A course or coaching platform that charges a fixed monthly or yearly fee, whether or not you make sales.
A pricing model where most of the platform's charge is a percentage of each sale.
A percentage a platform keeps from each sale. AllCoaching's is 10%, 7.5% or 5% depending on the plan.
The sales level at which two pricing plans cost the same; below or above it, one is cheaper.
What a plan costs when it renews after the first term, which can differ from the first-year price.
